text.insert: The event-driven librarian. It consumes one index_task, judges every touched subject against the material the task carries, and returns one librarian_pass_v1 proposal. It never writes the store: the apply layer validates every item and performs the writes. Model codex-lb/gpt-5.6-sol, thinking medium, runs in the background, no subagents.
The context packet names the current checkout head, the task, and its writable subjects. Canonical evidence and proposed-name reading views have separate sections.

props.title: Object by pathway

text.insert: The 11-tool librarian profile is knowledge_render_file, code_graph_search, graph_related_functions, discord_search, wiki_search, pr_search, attempt_search, knowledge_record, entity_lookup, resolve_locator, and unit_context. Every tool is read-only. Resolve and read each locator before citing it; search snippets and proposed names are not evidence.

props.description: One write or clear per subject and fact type. A write replaces the fact and its evidence. Evidence-backed relationships to entity subjects; duplicate links are skipped. Admissions and merges are restricted to game_concept and pattern. At most 10 out-of-scope subjects with a reason. The consumer enqueues accepted follow-ups as drift_recheck tasks.
props.name: Librarian Proposal

text.insert: New material can write or overwrite a fact. Confirmed material proposes nothing; a same-value write would replace the row. A task that teaches nothing still completes. Rename and drift audits are separate obligations: re-cite changed anchors at head, revise changed meaning, or clear unsupported claims. Run outcomes and scores remain attempt history. Events are never evidence.

steps.text: Claim the next queued index_task by pathway priority, then FIFO. Oversized PR, archival, and drift batches split before a model pass; the parent completes with child tasks.
Build the pathway context and run the model within the configured timeout, 900 seconds by default. Context or model failures release the claim and increment its persisted failure count.

Preview the proposal through apply. Rejected items return to the model for one correction turn; remaining rejected items are logged and dropped. For pr_imported, a discussion-comment citation must name the subject. A renamed subject or a flagged fact type may instead cite canonical code at head.

Apply entities, facts, links, and merges through the mechanical gates. Stamp every touched target; stamp an entity only when a fact or link landed on it. Enqueue accepted follow-ups. Recheck drift on pr_imported, run_closed, and drift_recheck; release once for unresolved drift, then complete with a warning if the retry still leaves drift.

At the next claim after two task failures, split a multi-item PR, drift, or archival task into smaller children. If it cannot split, complete it as abandoned and record a warning. More than five consecutive pass failures abort the drain; abandoned passes appear in summaries.

text.insert: : the write gates the apply layer enforces.
: the agent proposes and never writes. Every item passes shape validation, subject resolution, scope, citation resolution, and the pathway's citation rule before a row changes.
: the legacy librarian wrote the ledger directly from model output and the ledger filled with run history; one mechanical gate makes every knowledge path parseable and auditable.
: this agent, the backfill librarian, and any future knowledge writer.

: a librarian pass is scoped to the subjects its context named; a fact on a subject outside scope is rejected as out_of_scope, except on curated entities, which are always in scope under the shared gate.
: parallel lanes partition the store by scope; without it two passes could clobber each other's facts.
: the consumer's lanes and the backfill runner's lanes.

Decision: both librarians use applyLibrarianPass, but their injected schema files have different contracts. The event-driven schema includes follow_ups and entity-only link destinations; the backfill schema exposes four arrays and still permits target link destinations. Why: a shared validator does not make the prompts identical. Applies to: both schema files and any future reconciliation of their output guidance.
